token_contract.which: The token field of the canonical on-disk binding at crate::mcp::binding_path() - the exact file handshake_core capture_context reads. token_contract.refresh: No cache. Re-read on EVERY request, resolved as late as possible inside the async POST body on the off-frame dispatch worker (never the egui frame thread). Publication is an atomic replace, so a rebind with a new port/token/owning process is picked up by the very next event with no invalidation logic.
token_contract.absence: Typed EmitError::MissingSessionBinding{path,reason}; the POST is NOT attempted. A rejected credential is EmitError::SessionRejected{status,error_code} carrying the exact HSK-4xx-FR-* code. Never a silent drop.

ruling_401_vs_403_2026_09_17.question: MT-111 AC-111-2 and AC-111-4 (step 5) pin 401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION for a Flight Recorder request without a session token; the C-prime backend returns 403 HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE. Which is the contract?
spec_basis: Master Spec v02.206 §2.3.13.12.3 Authorization law (7): "Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists." (02-system-architecture.md)

Master Spec v02.206 §2.3.13.12.3 (2)+(6): every request authorizes Principal+session+action+exact resource; deny-by-default on every executable backend boundary. §2.3.13.12.4: Flight Recorder tables are protected resources and cannot become side-channel bypasses.
Codex [CX-132C] HARD_DENY_BY_DEFAULT_ACROSS_ALL_BOUNDARIES: missing/invalid/stale session context MUST deny (satisfied by both codes; does not choose the number).

The spec does NOT pin the numeric HTTP status for a missing credential; it pins the SHAPE (constant, non-distinguishing). A distinct 401 variant ahead of the protected-resource layer would be a second denial shape.
product_basis: src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/flight_recorder.rs::authorize_flight_recorder_request (line ~370) routes EVERY recorder request through api/authority.rs::authorize_request, which returns constant_denial() = 403 {error: HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE} for missing token, malformed token, missing channel binding, broker denial, and capability denial alike. unauthenticated_recorder() (401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION, flight_recorder.rs:96) is no longer reachable on that path.

The backend in-crate tests already pin the constant denial for the no-credential case: flight_recorder.rs ~4276 asserts "POST runtime_chat_event without binding" -> StatusCode::FORBIDDEN + HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE "must use the constant protected-resource denial"; ~4970 asserts unscoped/blank-scope reads -> 403 HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE.

ruling_401_vs_403_2026_09_17.ruling: SPEC WINS -> 403 HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE (constant-shape denial) is the contract for a Flight Recorder request that carries no/invalid session token, on both the ingest and the scoped-read side. This is NOT the spec-silent branch: §2.3.13.12.3(7) governs the denial shape, and the product authority layer plus its own pinned tests implement it. The 401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION wording in MT-111 AC-111-2 / AC-111-4 step 5 and in the flight_recorder.rs module doc-comment (line 10) is stale drift from before the protected-resource layer.

ruling_401_vs_403_confirmed.operator_semantics: Operator 2026-09-22 (relayed in the KERNEL_BUILDER-C1 brief): 401 = no valid authentication, 403 = authenticated but not permitted; keep the authority gate strict.
ruling_401_vs_403_confirmed.master_spec_clause: Master Spec v02.206 §2.3.13.12.3 Authorization law (7) (02-system-architecture.md): 'Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists.' + (2)/(6) deny-by-default per request. ruling_401_vs_403_confirmed.reconciliation: A uniform 401 emitted before any resource resolution (same body for every unauthenticated request, regardless of resource) discloses nothing about resource existence, so the Operator semantics satisfy (7). operator_decision.text: C1-FDELETE: deleting a workspace CASCADES to its rich documents, their version history and its Canvas boards. Only an owner/admin (capability-gated) may do it, and it emits an auditable Flight Recorder event. Version history stays immutable while the workspace exists; only whole-workspace deletion removes it.
operator_decision.spec_basis: No explicit Master Spec clause for this case (recorded as an Operator decision). Related: capability-gated auditable deletion (07-6 roadmap §11.5.12 reference; LM-RLS-001 admin role) and the ON DELETE CASCADE pattern for workspace-owned records.
